extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, patent searchers, inventors, and law students
extracted.subtask_description: A glossary-style collection of U.S. patentability standards, prosecution procedures, definitional terms, and related practice points used to evaluate and prosecute patent applications and patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level of Ordinary Skill
rubrics_metrics.description: The level of skill in the art to which an invention pertains that is used in judging whether a disclosure or claim is enabling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess enablement and obviousness (see: Enablement). MPEP 2141.03

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordinary Skill in the Art / Person Skilled in the Art
rubrics_metrics.description: A hypothetical person who has knowledge of all prior art and who possesses ordinary skill in the art to which the invention pertains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obviousness is measured with reference to this hypothetical person. See: Hypothetical Person Skilled in the Art. MPEP 2141.03

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentable Subject Matter (35 U.S.C. §101)
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention that is capable of being patented; includes statutory classes (machine, manufacture, composition of matter, process) while excluding products of nature and other unpatentable categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determines whether the invention type is eligible for patent protection. See: Machine, Manufacture, Product of Nature, Process. MPEP references vary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty (Anticipation)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the statutory requirements of patentability: what is considered 'new' about the invention; the invention must never have been made public in any way, anywhere, before the patent application date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novelty is normally determined by the date of the invention in the U.S. See: Obviousness, Utility. MPEP 2131

rubrics_metrics.name: Obviousness (Non-Obvious)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the statutory hurdles of patentability: whether the claimed invention would have been predictable to a person of ordinary skill in the art given the prior art (no 'inventive step').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obviousness is difficult to define; consider prior art body and level of ordinary skill. See: Novelty, Utility. MPEP 2141 and subparts. Secondary considerations (commercial success, long-felt need, unexpected results, failure of others, copying) are relevant evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary Considerations (Objective Evidence of Non-Obviousness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Objective evidence from the marketplace and surrounding circumstances relevant to whether an invention is non-obvious (e.g., commercial success, long-felt need, unexpected results, failure of others, copying).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to support non-obviousness determinations. See: Obviousness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-Felt Need
rubrics_metrics.description: A problem in a technical area that has gone unsolved for a prolonged period; its existence can support non-obviousness because if the solution were obvious others would have solved it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considered a secondary consideration in obviousness analysis. See: Obviousness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction to Practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Completion of the inventive process by physical verification that the invention works for its intended purpose (actual reduction) or constructive reduction by filing a patent application that adequately discloses the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actual reduction requires verification of each claimed element; degree depends on invention complexity. Constructive reduction occurs upon filing. MPEP 2138.05

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior Art (and Prior Art Reference)
rubrics_metrics.description: The body of prior knowledge relevant to the claimed invention (publications, prior use, patent disclosures). A prior art reference is a specific cited document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material to novelty and obviousness determinations. See relevant MPEP sections (2126–2128).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior Public Use / Public Use
rubrics_metrics.description: Display or use of an invention in circumstances that make it available to the public (as opposed to experimental use); such use before filing can bar patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public use is a statutory bar under U.S. law. See: Statutory Bar. MPEP 2133.01(a)

rubrics_metrics.name: On Sale / Public Sale / One-Year Rule (One-Year Grace Period)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an invention is offered for commercial sale more than one year before a U.S. patent application is filed, a valid patent cannot be obtained; the one-year rule allows filing within one year of public use, sale, patenting, or publication in the U.S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The on-sale bar and one-year grace period determine priority; reductions to practice and prior commercialization matter. See: One-Year Rule, Priority Date, MPEP 2133.03

rubrics_metrics.name: Paris Convention / Right of Priority / Priority Date
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Paris Convention, signatories have one year from first filing to file in other member countries and claim the original filing date as priority. Priority date is the initial filing date used to assess novelty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important for international filing strategy and claiming priority. See: MPEP 201.13 and related sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT) Timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: PCT preserves international filing rights for chapters: Chapter I preserves rights for 20 months from earliest priority filing; a timely Chapter II Demand preserves rights up to 30 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PCT for international designation and to defer national phase entries. See PCT provisions in MPEP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior Art Statement / Information Disclosure Statement (IDS)
rubrics_metrics.description: A document timely filed with the USPTO listing prior art known to applicant or counsel that is material to patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must disclose material prior art to the Office during prosecution. See: MPEP sections on IDS.

rubrics_metrics.name: New Matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Information not present in the original specification, claims, or drawings which an applicant attempts to add; such additions are rejected for not being present explicitly or implicitly in the original disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments cannot add new matter beyond original disclosure. MPEP 608.04 and subparts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Means-Plus-Function / Means for Claim
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim element recited as a means to accomplish a particular function (means-plus-function language).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Means claims are governed by specific rules (MPEP 2181); they are interpreted in view of disclosed structure that performs the function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markush Group
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim reciting 'selected from the group consisting of …' creating a limited generic claim; members must share at least one property primarily responsible for the claimed function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when claiming a set of alternatives sharing a common functional property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negative Limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim limitation that is exclusive (e.g., 'other than X', 'incapable of X'), also known as a negative claim limitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treated specially in claim interpretation and indefiniteness analyses. MPEP 2173.05(i)

rubrics_metrics.name: Prolix Claim
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim containing long recitations or unimportant details that renders the claim indefinite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid excessive, unimportant detail in claims to prevent indefiniteness. MPEP 2173.05(m)

rubrics_metrics.name: Preamble (of a Claim)
rubrics_metrics.description: The formal introductory clause of a patent claim which may or may not define a narrowing element of the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preamble usually defines context; Jepson claim preambles imply admission of prior art and may affect claim scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product per se Claim / Product-by-Process Claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Product per se: a claim to the physical form of an invention irrespective of production method. Product-by-process: a claim that describes a product by the process used to make it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Product-by-process claims are interpreted based on product identity; claiming product by process can have limits in effect and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product of Nature (Unpatentable)
rubrics_metrics.description: A thing occurring naturally that is substantially unaltered by human intervention is not patentable (e.g., raw natural products); genetically engineered or pure cultures may not be products of nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether human intervention has created a patentable distinction. MPEP 706.03(a), MPEP 2105

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility / New Use
rubrics_metrics.description: Discovery of a new use for a previous invention can be patentable subject matter under U.S. law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims to new, practical utility can support patentability when properly disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of Validity and Burden of Proof
rubrics_metrics.description: A statutory presumption that an issued patent is legitimate; the challenger bears the burden to prove invalidity by clear and convincing evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important in litigation and post-grant challenges; affects evidentiary standards for invalidity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prima Facie
rubrics_metrics.description: Sufficient evidence on its face to raise the presumption of fact unless rebutted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in prosecution and evidentiary contexts (see MPEP 2001).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection / Office Action
rubrics_metrics.description: An Examiner's refusal of a patent application or individual claims (rejection). Office Actions communicate such rejections or objections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may amend claims, argue, request reconsideration, or appeal rejections. See relevant MPEP sections (e.g., 706).

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Reconsideration / Request for Reexamination / Request for Reexamination (by third party)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural filings to seek further argument after rejection or to ask the Office (or third parties to ask) to reexamine patentability in light of new printed prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests have specific bases and procedural requirements (MPEP 714.13, 818.03, 1214.01, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: An application filed by a patentee after grant to correct errors in the issued patent that render it wholly or partly inoperative, or to correct claims that are too broad or too narrow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must surrender the issued patent provisionally; reissue patents keep original expiration date. MPEP 1401–1403

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination of the patentability of issued patent claims at the request of the USPTO, the patent owner, or a third party to introduce newly discovered prior art/printed publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanism to revisit patentability post-issuance. MPEP 2209–2210

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction Requirement (Restriction)
rubrics_metrics.description: An Examiner's requirement that an applicant elect which of multiple distinct inventions claimed in an application to pursue for examination; nonelected claims may be pursued in a divisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond by election or file divisional applications. MPEP 802–803

rubrics_metrics.name: Prosecution / Prosecution History
rubrics_metrics.description: The administrative process of obtaining a patent (filing, office actions, amendments, interviews, appeals, fee payments) and the documentary history of that process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prosecution history can affect claim interpretation and estoppel issues (e.g., prosecution history estoppel).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prosecution History Estoppel / File Wrapper Estoppel
rubrics_metrics.description: Doctrines limiting claim scope in litigation based on arguments or amendments made during patent prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims surrendered during prosecution may prevent recapture of scope in enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation and Revival (Abandonment / Revival / Petition to Revive)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures to revive abandoned applications or restore lapsed patents (reinstatement) due to failure to take required actions or nonpayment of fees, often via petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions may be for unavoidable or unintentional abandonment; revival has specific grounds and MPEP references (e.g., 711, maintenance/renewal fees).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Misuse / Misuse
rubrics_metrics.description: Using a patent right inappropriately (e.g., forcing a buyer to take a license on an unrelated product), which can limit enforcement rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can be raised as a defense in infringement proceedings; affects equitable relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Marking / Notice (Marking)
rubrics_metrics.description: Affixing 'patent' and patent numbers (or 'patent pending') on products or packaging to give notice; failure to mark may limit damages recovery to dates after actual notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper marking provides constructive notice; absence of marking can restrict recovery of damages until actual notice. See: Patent Marking, Notice, MPEP references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability / Rationale for Patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: The determination and reasoning whether a claimed invention meets legal requirements for patent grant (novelty, non-obviousness, utility, statutory subject matter, enablement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale often documented in office actions and MPEP guidance (e.g., MPEP 1302.14).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Search / Search Report
rubrics_metrics.description: A review of prior art (patents and non-patent literature) to assess patentability; a search report lists references and presents an opinion on patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Searches inform drafting and prosecution strategy; search reports can be prepared by patent searchers or the Examiner. See MPEP 707.05, 1844.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability Opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: An opinion provided by a patent agent or attorney assessing whether a claimed invention is likely to be deemed patentable in view of known prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisory for prosecution and filing strategy; relies on available prior art and legal standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent office rules governing format and presentation of nucleotide/amino acid sequence data in applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow sequence submission rules (MPEP 2420–2421.02) to ensure proper filing and examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Allowance / Notice of Allowance and Issue Fee
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO communications that an application is allowed and that issue/printing fees must be paid within a set period (typically three months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow payment deadlines to obtain grant. See MPEP 1303.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals (Notice of Appeal / Appeal Brief)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Notice of Appeal initiates an appeal from an Examiner's rejection to the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences and reserves the right to file an Appeal Brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow procedural rules for appeals (MPEP 1205 and related sections).
